question: The core of a transformer is constructed by stacking thin sheets of soft iron (laminations) insulated from each other, rather than using a solid block of iron. What is the specific physical reason for this construction?

options.A: To increase the magnetic saturation limit of the core.
options.B: To increase the electrical resistance of the core path, thereby reducing Eddy Currents.
options.C: To increase the surface area for cooling.
options.D: To make the transformer lighter and cheaper.
